canonical_question: Why was 1210 °C for 10 h specifically selected for solution-heat-treatment to homogenize chemical segregations rather than a different temperature or time?

answers.answer: The solution-heat-treatment (SHT) was conducted at 1210 °C for 10 h to homogenize chemical segregations. The text does not provide the specific rationale for why these exact parameters were selected.
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparative data or rationale for alternative temperatures/times provided.
evidence_spans: The design of HESA was also assisted by CALPHAD-based simulation (JMatPro [55] , Ni-alloys database), and the aim is to contain more than 60 vol% of strengthening L1 2 γ′ as commercial Ni-based superalloys.

Furthermore, since the addition of refractory elements can easily promote the formation of detrimental topological-close packed (TCP) phases, the fraction of TCP was designed to be less than 1 vol% while adjusting the refractory additions.
